As the tide recedes, a large shell rises out of a tidal pool, a single orange eye peering across the receding waves, searching for the 
flopping desperation of stranded fi sh. Suddenly, a tail whips salt water into the air and with loping limbs the large snail strides across 
the sands. Quickly, out pacing competing crustaceans, it grasps the fi sh with its four prehensile tentacles, pulling the live prey in and 
grinding flesh and bone whole into its fearsome maw. Over time, gharril slowly build up a pearl of sorts in their gullet, a rolled and 
compressed sphere of bone and chitin from their coastal feasting. When threatened by a larger predator, they can expel this organic 
cannonball with devastating velocity, shattering bone and shell alike.
Class - Gastropoda • Genus Derived Evolution - Euglandina • Niche - Amphibious Generalist Omnivore
Preyed upon by - Cerrophol, Daellash, Illithisk, Slannethiss • Preys on - Daugon, Lanceleth, Scavick, Vinnirex
Encountering While hunting along the many tidal pools during 
the day, gharril are generally aggressively territorial. Th ough 
when the suns sets, they calm down to settle into the sand to 
conserve heat as their soft fleshed bodies are poorly adapted to 
withstand the cold. If discovered at night, this creature will put 
up little fi ght as it takes time for warmth to suffuse its limbs.

Slobbering Maw If a gharril is Grappling a creature it can wrap 
its tentacles around the target’s head as a Bonus Action, dealing 
3 (1d6) Piercing damage. Wisdom Saving Th row: DC 13, the creature 
currently Grappled. Failure: Th e target has the Frightened 
condition until the start of its next turn.

After a season of predation and scavenging, 
their gullet amasses a condensed spherical 
pearl comprised of bone and chitin
AmphibiousA gharril can breathe both air and water.
Coral Shelled When a gharril’s lower body is buried and remains 
motionless, it is indistinguishable from a coral outcropping. It 
has advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks made to Hide while in 
the Strands biome or coastal-like environments.
Resistances Bludgeoning
Defensive Instinct (1/Day) If it survives any attempt at being attacked 
for the fi rst time the gharril will attempt to bury its more vulnerable soft 
flesh in the sand. 
On its turn, the gharril lowers its movement speed to 0 ft., loses 
its Vulnerability to Cold and gains +2 AC (total 17). It can choose to 
return to its normal state as a Bonus action.
